To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phosphorylation by PKC is required to achieve maximal stimulation of the cystic fibrocis transmembrane conductanceregulator (CFTR) by PKA.
the PKC-mediated phosphorylation of CFTR is essential for acute PKA activation of CFTR in transfected Chinese hamaster ovary (CHO) cells.
PKA-mediated activation of the cystic fibro- sis transmembrane conduct- ance regulator requires PKC phosphorylation of CFTR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PKC phosphorylation of CFTR in the acute regulation of channel function by PKA.
the role of PKC phosphorylation of CFTR in the acute activation of the channel by PKA.
the role of protein kinase C (PCK) in the activation of the CFTR chloride channels in response to cAMP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PKA-mediated activation of CFTR is dependent on PKC phosphorylation.
the PKA-mediated phosphorylations of CFTR alone are not sufficient to activate the CFTR channel in the presence or absence of MgATP.
phosphorylation by PKA alone is not sufficient to open the CF TR chloride channel in the absence of constitutive PKC activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PKC is required for acute activation of the CFTR channel by PKA, but not for the maintenance of channel activation.
PKA and PKC phosphorylate the same residues on CFTR but that PKC is required for the acute response to PKA in intact cells.
PKA-mediated activation of CFTR requires a constitutive phosphorylation of the channel by PKC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PKC and PKA act synergistically to activate the CFTR channel, and that PKC is required for acute stimulation of the CFTR channel by cAMP.
PKC activity is required for acute stimulation of CF.
PKC activity is required for PKA-mediated stimulation of CFTR.
